stem: A registrar receives a genomic result first and then re-examines the child to see whether the physical findings match that result; what is this process called?
explanation: Reverse phenotyping is the process of starting with a genomic result and then reviewing the phenotype to see whether it fits.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Genetics

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because cascade screening refers to testing relatives in a family after an index case is identified.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because reverse phenotyping starts with genomic information and then re-examines the child’s phenotype for features that match the result.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because serial surveillance means ongoing monitoring over time, not matching a genomic result to clinical findings.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because genotype masking is not the term for reviewing the phenotype after a genomic finding.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because targeted counselling may be part of clinical care, but it is not the process of matching genotype back to phenotype.
